parameterMap.note: Current mapping for deploy/main.bicep and deploy/azuredeploy.json as read on 2026-10-06. Keep this section in sync when the template parameter list changes.

patterns.label: North Star pooled host pool
patterns.reason: Use the North Star when the workload can run on pooled Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session hosts with Microsoft Entra join, Intune, App Attach and FSLogix.

patterns.label: Two host pools with a hybrid-joined legacy pool
patterns.reason: Use a separate hybrid-joined stepping-stone pool when applications need AD DS machine authentication or other domain-joined behaviour.

patterns.label: Personal desktops or Windows 365 for dedicated users
patterns.reason: Use dedicated desktops only for personas that genuinely need persistence, local tools or stronger separation.

patterns.label: RemoteApp for application-only access
patterns.reason: Use RemoteApp when users need published applications without a full desktop.

patterns.label: Multi-region recovery pattern
patterns.reason: Use a secondary region when recovery objectives require a regional failover path for profiles, applications, images and host pool configuration.

patterns.label: Private connectivity pattern
patterns.reason: Use private endpoints and controlled outbound connectivity where the network design requires private access to profile and application shares.

decisions.label: Host pool type
decisions.rule: Pooled for shared desktops and RemoteApp. Personal host pools are a separate pattern for dedicated desktops.

decisions.label: Management approach
decisions.rule: Session host configuration is fixed at host pool creation and cannot be added later.

decisions.label: Join type per pool
decisions.rule: Host pools should contain only VMs of the same domain join type.

dependencies.label: Microsoft Entra authentication for RDP and single sign-on
Intune tenant, policies and multi-session targeting
Required FQDNs, endpoints and outbound path
Azure Files identity, private endpoints and DNS
Azure Image Builder and Azure Compute Gallery pipeline
Session host configuration and dynamic autoscaling
Application inventory and App Attach candidates

questions.label: Organisation name
questions.why: Used only to label the workshop report and tags in the generated pilot parameters.

questions.label: Short workload prefix
questions.why: This feeds resource names in the Deploy to Azure template.

questions.label: Primary Azure region for the pilot
questions.why: Region choice affects latency, quota, storage locality and availability zones.

questions.label: Pilot users group object ID
questions.why: The template assigns pilot users through a Microsoft Entra group rather than individual users.

questions.label: Named users in scope
questions.why: Named users set licence and migration scope, but sizing uses peak concurrent users.

questions.label: Peak concurrent users for the pilot or first wave
questions.why: Session host estimates use peak concurrency divided by tested sessions per host.

questions.label: Where do users work from?
questions.why: Network ownership and distance drive RDP Shortpath, proxy and latency testing.

questions.label: Describe the main arrival waves and time zones
questions.default: Contoso Australia starts around 08:00, with a smaller support wave at 13:00.
questions.why: Autoscale schedules work best when host pools are segmented by usage pattern and time zone.

questions.label: Primary delivery model
questions.why: Application groups decide whether users see desktops, RemoteApp applications or both.

questions.label: Do any users need dedicated persistent desktops?
questions.why: Dedicated desktops are a stepping stone or separate pattern, not the pooled North Star.

questions.label: Do developers need persistent desktops, local tools or elevated rights?
questions.why: Developer desktops can change the choice between pooled AVD, personal host pools and Windows 365.

questions.label: Is there an application inventory with owners and validation groups?
questions.why: Application ownership and validation evidence decide what can move to App Attach or a stepping stone.

questions.label: Number of App-V packages
questions.why: App Attach can use App-V packages as a bridge while MSIX packaging matures.

questions.label: Number of MSIX or Appx packages already available
questions.why: MSIX and Appx packages are the preferred App Attach format for Windows 11.

questions.label: Number of installed applications in the current image
questions.why: A high installed-app count usually means the image needs a parallel simplification stream.

questions.label: Do any applications need AD DS machine authentication?
questions.why: Microsoft Entra joined devices do not support on-premises applications that rely on machine authentication.

questions.label: Known NTLM dependency
questions.why: NTLMv1 dependencies need early remediation before modern Windows images are adopted.

questions.label: Which legacy traits are present?
questions.why: Application traits affect pool segmentation, image content, App Attach suitability and media testing.

questions.label: User identity model

options.label: Hybrid identities synchronised from AD DS

questions.why: The identity model affects sign-in, FSLogix, Kerberos and external user requirements.

questions.label: Do session hosts need line of sight to AD DS for applications or resources?
questions.why: Entra joined hosts can be deployed without a domain controller, but on-premises resources may still require AD DS reachability.

questions.label: Is Microsoft Entra authentication for RDP and AVD single sign-on ready?
questions.why: Single sign-on removes the session host credential prompt and changes Conditional Access scope.

questions.label: Are Conditional Access licences and policies ready for AVD and Windows Cloud Login?
questions.why: Conditional Access is the entry-control layer for feed access and session host sign-in.

questions.label: Do in-scope users have AVD, Intune and required Entra licences?
questions.why: Licensing needs to be confirmed before the pilot is treated as deployable.

questions.label: Is Intune ready to manage Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session hosts?
questions.why: The North Star enrols Entra joined session hosts in Intune during provisioning.

questions.label: Do existing virtual desktop policies need to be reviewed or reset?
questions.why: Inherited Group Policy or legacy platform policy can hide North Star dependency gaps.

questions.label: Is Configuration Manager used for images, applications or updates today?
questions.why: Existing management tooling may require a temporary image or standard-management stepping stone.

questions.label: Image starting point for the pilot

options.label: Parallel clean and existing image tracks

questions.why: Microsoft's image guidance recommends starting from a new source VM, while an existing image can be a time-bound stepping stone.

questions.label: Is an Azure Image Builder and Azure Compute Gallery pipeline ready?
questions.why: The North Star treats the image pipeline as the source of truth for disposable hosts.

questions.label: Should the Marketplace image include Microsoft 365 Apps?
questions.why: The Deploy to Azure template chooses between Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session image families.

questions.label: Marketplace image version

validation.invalidMessage: Enter an exact Marketplace image version such as 26300.9457.260914, or leave this blank so the generated commands look up the newest version. Do not enter latest.

questions.why: The template needs an exact version, not latest. Find it with Azure CLI: az vm image list -l <region> -p MicrosoftWindowsDesktop -f <offer> -s <sku> --all --query "[-1].version" -o tsv. Or use PowerShell: Get-AzVMImage -Location <region> -PublisherName MicrosoftWindowsDesktop -Offer <offer> -Skus <sku>.

questions.label: Will the pilot host pool be created with session host configuration?
questions.why: The host pool management approach is fixed at creation and cannot be changed later.

questions.label: Session host VM size
questions.why: The deployment template only allows these v5 sizes because their temporary disk can hold the 127 GiB Windows 11 image as an ephemeral OS disk.

questions.label: Host pool metadata deployment scope
questions.why: Regional host pools use separate backend infrastructure and are only available in supported regions, so use Geographical unless Regional is explicitly selected.

questions.label: Session host name prefix
questions.why: The current deployment template maps this to the session host computer name prefix.

questions.label: Tested or target sessions per host
questions.why: This drives the host estimate and must be validated with real workloads.

questions.label: Capacity headroom percentage
questions.why: Headroom absorbs logon storms, uneven placement and host maintenance.

questions.label: Ramp-up minimum host pool size
questions.why: The pilot scaling plan needs a minimum floor for user experience and testing.

questions.label: Ramp-up maximum host pool size
questions.why: The maximum host pool size caps dynamic scale-out during the pilot.

questions.label: Ramp-down minimum host pool size
questions.why: A zero off-peak floor is a cost choice that must be balanced against first-user wait time.

questions.label: Ramp-down maximum host pool size
questions.why: This caps off-peak capacity during the pilot scaling schedule.

questions.label: Scaling plan time zone
questions.why: Scaling plans use a configured time zone, so multiple arrival waves may need separate pools.

questions.label: Use availability zones for pilot hosts if the region and SKU support them?
questions.why: Availability zones improve in-region resiliency when supported by the region and VM SKU.

questions.label: Is FSLogix used today?
questions.why: Existing FSLogix use can accelerate profile migration but storage identity and sizing still need validation.

questions.label: Average profile size in GB
questions.why: Capacity matters, but the first sizing pass also needs IOPS at sign-in and steady state.

questions.label: Azure Files share model for estimates
questions.why: Azure Files IOPS limits differ by share model and media tier.

questions.label: Is Azure Files identity for FSLogix ready?
questions.why: The North Star uses Azure Files SMB with Microsoft Entra Kerberos for FSLogix access.

questions.label: Is the subscription, landing zone and quota ready?
questions.why: The platform needs subscription placement, quota, network and governance before session hosts scale.

questions.label: Use an existing hub, spoke and session host subnet?
questions.why: The Deploy to Azure template can create a new network or use an existing subnet.

questions.label: Existing session host subnet resource ID
questions.why: Needed only when the pilot deploys into an existing subnet.

questions.label: New virtual network address prefix
questions.why: Used when the pilot creates a new virtual network.

questions.label: New session host subnet prefix
questions.why: Used when the pilot creates a new session host subnet.

questions.label: Can session hosts reach required AVD, Entra, Intune and Azure endpoints?
questions.why: AVD depends on outbound access to required FQDNs and service endpoints.

questions.label: Session host outbound method
questions.why: The North Star prefers explicit outbound connectivity rather than implicit default outbound access.

questions.label: Use private endpoints for Azure Files profile and app shares?
questions.why: Private endpoints keep SMB access to profile and application shares on private IPs.

questions.label: Can clients and firewalls support RDP Shortpath UDP where policy allows?
questions.why: RDP Shortpath can improve reliability and latency when UDP paths are available.

questions.label: Are secure web gateways, proxies or SSL inspection in the path?
questions.why: Proxy and inspection policy can affect AVD, Teams media optimisation, Intune and storage access.

questions.label: Do users connect from networks the organisation does not control?
questions.why: Uncontrolled networks need explicit testing for RDP Shortpath, proxies and client experience.

questions.label: Clipboard policy needed
questions.why: Clipboard direction and data-type controls are part of the data protection baseline.

questions.label: Which redirections are required?
questions.why: Peripheral redirection should be denied by default and allowed by exception.

questions.label: Need screen capture protection?
questions.why: Screen capture protection is useful for sensitive pools and should be tested with client platforms.

questions.label: Need watermarking?
questions.why: Watermarking helps trace leaked screen content for high-risk personas.

questions.label: Do any users need local administrator rights in-session?
questions.why: Local admin needs usually indicate a dedicated-desktop or privilege-management stream.

questions.label: Is Log Analytics, AVD diagnostics and AVD Insights ready?
questions.why: The North Star turns on diagnostics and Insights from the first pilot host pool.

questions.label: Number of people who will operate AVD day to day
questions.why: Team size and skills determine how much automation, runbook detail and partner support are needed.

questions.label: Current operations skills
questions.why: Skills shape the migration plan, support model and handover requirements.

questions.label: Will a partner operate or support the platform?
questions.why: Partner involvement changes access, runbooks, knowledge transfer and accountability.

questions.label: Recovery time objective in hours
questions.why: RTO decides whether active-passive regional recovery is enough or whether a warmer design is needed.

questions.label: Recovery point objective in hours
questions.why: RPO drives profile, package and image replication or backup choices.

questions.label: Is a secondary Azure region required?
questions.why: Regional recovery is a separate design for profiles, packages, images, identity and application routing.

questions.label: Is there a per-persona cost baseline to compare against?
questions.why: A baseline prevents average cost from hiding expensive personas or peak capacity.

questions.label: Commitment strategy for compute

options.label: Savings plan or reservation for measured baseline only

questions.why: Commitments can reduce unit cost but may fight Autoscale if they cover removable peak capacity.

questions.label: Should the template assign autoscale roles to the host pool managed identity?
questions.why: Dynamic autoscaling creates session hosts through the host pool managed identity, so it needs subscription-scope Desktop Virtualization autoscale roles.

questions.label: Does the Azure Virtual Desktop service principal already have the autoscale roles at subscription scope?
questions.why: Only assign these roles to the service principal when they are absent. Duplicate Azure role assignments can fail the deployment.

questions.label: Azure Virtual Desktop service principal object ID, if required
questions.why: The current template accepts this for optional autoscale role assignments.

questions.label: Azure Virtual Desktop ARM Provider service principal object ID, if required
questions.why: The current template accepts this for Azure Files App Attach access.

questions.label: Pilot local administrator username
questions.why: The parameter file includes the username, but never includes the password.

questions.label: Target pilot start date
questions.why: Dates help identify which dependencies are on the critical path.

questions.label: Architecture or security governance gate before pilot?
questions.why: Governance gates decide when the generated pilot parameters become a deployable plan.

questions.label: Decision date for moving from pilot to production design
questions.why: A named decision date keeps stepping stones temporary and evidence-driven.

questions.label: Open risks, blockers or assumptions
questions.default: Contoso needs to confirm quota, App Attach candidates and the Conditional Access pilot policy.
questions.why: Capturing assumptions makes the discovery output useful after the workshop.
